sections.title: Grade 4 skills
sections.description: The most important words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 4.

sections.title: Grade 3 skills
sections.description: Key words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 3.

questions.question: Which word means ‘a person who belongs to a country and has rights there’?
questions.explanation: A citizen belongs to a country and has rights there. A tenant rents a home, and a merchant buys and sells goods.

questions.question: Which word means ‘the hard work you put into doing something’?
questions.explanation: Effort is the hard work you put into a task. Rest and leisure are about relaxing, the opposite idea.

questions.question: Which word means ‘to run fast on four legs, like a horse’?
questions.explanation: Gallop means to run fast on four legs. A signal is a sign that tells you something, not a way of moving.

questions.question: Sami keeps asking questions about how the old clock works. Which word describes him?
questions.explanation: A curious person really wants to know or learn something new, just like Sami with the clock.

questions.question: Which word means ‘happy to share what you have with other people’?
questions.explanation: A generous person is happy to share or give to others. Selfish means the opposite — only caring about yourself.

questions.question: Read the text. ‘Every morning Omar sorts the mail and weighs the parcels at the market shop. He checks each address twice, because one mistake could send a letter to the wrong street.’ Why does Omar check each address twice?
questions.options: So a letter does not go to the wrong street | So the parcels weigh less | So the shop opens on time | So the mail arrives late
questions.correctAnswer: So a letter does not go to the wrong street
questions.explanation: The text says one mistake could send a letter to the wrong street, so Omar checks carefully to stop that happening.

questions.question: Read the text. ‘Omar speaks two languages at his shop, so he can serve almost every customer in town, whichever language they use.’ What can we tell about the customers who visit Omar’s shop?
questions.options: They speak more than one language between them | They all speak exactly the same language | None of them can understand Omar | They never need any help
questions.correctAnswer: They speak more than one language between them
questions.explanation: Omar needs two languages to serve almost everyone, so his customers must use more than one language between them.

questions.question: Read the text. ‘Before Amal, Leo and Nora went into the tunnel, they checked that it was safe. First they moved slowly towards the cave, and then they checked for loose stones.’ What did the children do first?
questions.options: They moved slowly towards the cave | They checked for loose stones | They ran straight into the tunnel | They carried the stones away
questions.correctAnswer: They moved slowly towards the cave
questions.explanation: The word First tells us the order: moving towards the cave happened before checking for loose stones.

questions.question: Read the text. ‘Runners often accelerate near the finish line, because that final burst of speed can win the race.’ Why do runners accelerate near the finish line?
questions.options: Because going faster there can help them win | Because they feel tired by then | Because the crowd asks them to stop | Because the race is already over
questions.correctAnswer: Because going faster there can help them win
questions.explanation: The text says a final burst of speed near the line can win the race, which is why runners accelerate there.

questions.question: Read the text. ‘Amal felt nervous before the school play, but her friend Sami reminded her that everyone gets nervous before something new.’ What does Sami’s reminder suggest about feeling nervous?
questions.options: It is a normal feeling before something new | It only happens to Amal | It means the play will go badly | It is a sign that Amal should give up
questions.correctAnswer: It is a normal feeling before something new
questions.explanation: Sami says everyone gets nervous before something new, which shows the feeling is normal and shared, not just Amal’s.

questions.question: Choose the correct question: ‘______ does she like to do after school?’
questions.explanation: What asks about a thing or activity, so ‘What does she like to do’ is the natural question here.

questions.question: Which sentence gives a clear instruction?
questions.options: Close the window, please. | You closing the window. | Closes the window. | Window the close.
questions.explanation: An instruction starts with the base verb and leaves out the word you: ‘Close the window, please.’

questions.question: Choose the correct past form: ‘Last Saturday we ______ a little cave near the bay.’
questions.explanation: Find is an irregular verb, so it changes shape instead of adding -ed: find becomes found.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence: ‘You ______ check that the cave is safe before going in.’
questions.explanation: Must shows a rule that really matters, and the verb after it stays plain: ‘You must check.’

questions.question: Choose the correct present perfect form: ‘She has never ______ mango juice before.’
questions.explanation: The present perfect uses have or has with the past participle, and the past participle of try is tried.

questions.question: Which connective best completes this sentence? ‘I wanted to go outside, ______ it started to rain.’
questions.explanation: But shows a difference between two ideas — wanting to go outside and the rain stopping you.

questions.question: In a set of instructions, which word usually signals the very last step?
questions.explanation: Finally tells the reader they have reached the last step, after First, Then and After that.

questions.question: A fact file about a person’s job should begin with which kind of sentence?
questions.options: A clear heading that names the topic | A question with no answer | A list of unrelated facts | An apology for mistakes
questions.correctAnswer: A clear heading that names the topic
questions.explanation: A fact file starts with a clear heading, like ‘The Post Counter’, so the reader instantly knows the topic.

questions.question: Which sentence punctuates the spoken words correctly?
questions.options: “I agree with your plan,” said Maya. | I agree with your plan, said Maya. | “I agree with your plan” said Maya. | I agree with your plan” said Maya.
questions.correctAnswer: “I agree with your plan,” said Maya.
questions.explanation: Speech marks wrap the exact words spoken, and a comma sits inside them before the closing mark.

questions.question: Which word means ‘to finish school or a class’?
questions.explanation: To graduate is to finish school or a class. To prepare is to get ready, and to study is to learn.

questions.question: Which word means ‘liked by many people’?
questions.explanation: Popular means liked by many people. Careless means not paying enough attention.

questions.question: Which word describes someone who thinks carefully about other people’s feelings?
questions.explanation: A thoughtful person thinks carefully about how others feel. Enjoyable describes something fun, not a person’s character.

questions.question: Read the text. ‘The class prepared all week for the grammar contest. On the day, Nadia felt proud when her team won first place.’ How did Nadia feel when her team won?
questions.explanation: The text says Nadia felt proud when her team won first place in the contest.

questions.question: Read the text. ‘Nora saw a boy trip and fall near the school gate. She was kind, so she stopped to help him up and carried his bag.’ Why did Nora help the boy?
questions.options: Because she is kind | Because the teacher told her to | Because the bag was hers | Because she wanted a reward
questions.explanation: The text says Nora was kind, so, showing that her kindness is the reason she stopped to help.

questions.question: Read the text. ‘Sami had one idea for the class box, but he kept it hidden all morning because he felt shy about sharing it.’ Why did Sami keep his idea hidden?
questions.options: Because he felt shy about sharing it | Because the idea was not his | Because the box was already full | Because his idea was hopeless
questions.correctAnswer: Because he felt shy about sharing it
questions.explanation: The text gives the reason directly: Sami felt shy about sharing his idea, so he kept it hidden.

questions.question: Choose the correct past tense: ‘We ______ rice for dinner last night.’
questions.explanation: Eat is an irregular verb, so its past form changes shape instead of adding -ed: eat becomes ate.

questions.question: Compare the two stories: ‘This story is ______ than the last one.’
questions.explanation: Funny ends in -y, so the y changes to i before -er: funnier. Funniest compares three or more things.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence: ‘Tomorrow we ______ share more ideas in class.’
questions.explanation: Will points to the future, so it is the right choice for a plan happening tomorrow.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly gives a reason using ‘because’?
questions.options: We went to the library because we wanted quiet books. | We went to the library it because we wanted quiet books. | Because we went to the library we wanted quiet books it. | We went to the library, we wanted quiet books because.
questions.correctAnswer: We went to the library because we wanted quiet books.
questions.explanation: Because sits between the idea and the reason that explains it: the result first, then because, then the reason.

questions.question: A paragraph comparing two people should mostly use which kind of sentence?
questions.options: Sentences that show how the two people are alike and different | Sentences that only describe one person | A list of random facts with no order | Sentences written as questions only
questions.correctAnswer: Sentences that show how the two people are alike and different
questions.explanation: A comparing paragraph works by showing likenesses and differences between the two people, one point at a time.

questions.question: Which is the best opening for a short report about a person?
questions.options: A heading that names the person and what they do | A joke that has nothing to do with the topic | The very last fact from the report | A list of the writer’s own hobbies
questions.correctAnswer: A heading that names the person and what they do
questions.explanation: A short report opens with a heading that names the person and their role, so the reader knows the topic at once.

questions.question: Before writing about how you prepared for something, what should you plan first?
questions.options: The order of the steps you took | The very last sentence only | A made-up ending | Words with no connection to the topic
questions.correctAnswer: The order of the steps you took
questions.explanation: A ‘how I prepared’ piece works best when the steps are planned in order, so the reader can follow what happened first, next and last.
